title: Kioxia Announces GP2 Series SSD with Over 18 Million Random Read IOPS
gist: Kioxia announced the GP2 Series SSD (PCIe 6.0 / NVMe 2.3, XL-FLASH gen 3) with >18M random read IOPS at 512B, nearly double the GP1, aimed at a GPU-accessible flash memory tier that substitutes for costlier HBM/DRAM in AI systems. Evaluation samples only reach select customers by end of 2027, so it is a longer-dated roadmap item.

insights.claim: Kioxia's GP2 Series SSD delivers more than 18 million random read IOPS at a 512-byte block size, nearly double the GP1 Series shown at FMS in August 2026, with expected sequential reads up to 28GB/s on PCIe 6.0 / NVMe 2.3.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Small-block IOPS is roughly doubling per generation in AI-oriented SSDs; a benchmark to track Kioxia against rival flash vendors.
insights.quote: 18M IOPS is nearly double the performance of the GP1 Series Kioxia showed in August at FMS.

insights.claim: Kioxia says the GP2's XL-FLASH generation 3 memory delivers about 2.5x the IOPS of its own TLC-based CM10 Series SSDs at a 512-byte block size, plus higher endurance, because low-latency flash better suits fine-grained memory-expansion access than TLC.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Specialty low-latency NAND (XL-FLASH) is being positioned as a distinct product line from capacity TLC, potentially higher-margin.
insights.locator: Kioxia is using its XL-FLASH generation 3

insights.claim: Kioxia's GP series is designed to let AI operators build a flash-based memory tier that GPUs access directly, instead of adding more expensive HBM or DRAM, handling larger datasets at lower cost.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: If GPU-attached flash tiers gain adoption, some AI memory spend could shift from HBM/DRAM toward specialty NAND; watch for hyperscaler qualification.
insights.quote: Instead of adding more expensive HBM or DRAM to a GPU system, operators can use these NAND-based drives to create a flash-based memory tier the GPU can access directly.

insights.claim: Endurance is the key question when replacing DRAM with NAND; the Kioxia GP2 is rated up to 50 DWPD, a step above many common capacity-focused SSDs.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Endurance ratings are the gating spec for NAND-as-memory adoption; 50 DWPD is the bar to compare competitors against.
insights.quote: Whenever you try to replace DRAM with NAND, endurance becomes a question.

insights.claim: Kioxia previewed a 20M IOPS GP-series system live at OCP Summit 2026 and says future generations will target up to 100 million random read IOPS.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Signals a multi-generation roadmap for AI-memory flash, but the 100M IOPS target is aspirational.
insights.quote: future generations will target up to 100 million random read IOPS, but we are not there just yet
insights.locator: Kioxia GP Series SSD preview at OCP Summit 2026

insights.claim: Kioxia GP2 evaluation samples will reach only select customers by the end of 2027, making the product a distant revenue contributor even as AMD and NVIDIA PCIe Gen6 systems begin appearing.
insights.speaker: Cliff Robinson
insights.so_what: Do not expect GP2 revenue before 2028; PCIe Gen6 platform ramps are the nearer-term enabler to watch.
insights.quote: evaluation GP2 samples will be available to select customers by the end of 2027, so this seems a bit further out
